title: Do Center Biases Propagate? Robustness of Pathology Foundation Models in Whole-Slide Image Classification
abstract: arXiv:2609.28231v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) have transformed computational pathology through powerful representation learning from histopathological images. PFMs provide rich, discriminative representations for whole slide image (WSI) analysis, enabling tasks such as slide-level classification under multiple instance learning (MIL). However, these representations may also encode non-biological signals associated with acquisition centers, potentially introducing spurious shortcuts into downstream predictions. In this work, we evaluate center-associated robustness in WSI classification using a controlled training setting with increasing class-center correlations quantified by Cram\'er's V. We benchmark six PFMs across four datasets and two MIL aggregators, while evaluating ComBat as a robustification strategy. translated_title: 中心偏置会传播吗？病理学基础模型在全切片图像分类中的鲁棒性
translated_abstract: 病理学基础模型（PFMs）通过对组织病理学图像的强大表示学习，变革了计算病理学领域。PFMs为全切片图像（WSI）分析提供了丰富且具有判别力的表示，支持在多实例学习（MIL）框架下进行切片级分类等任务。然而，这些表示也可能编码与采集中心相关的非生物学信号，从而可能在下游预测中引入虚假的捷径。在本工作中，我们使用一种受控训练设置来评估WSI分类中与中心相关的鲁棒性，该设置通过Cramér's V来量化递增的类别-中心相关性。我们在四个数据集和两种MIL聚合器上对六种PFMs进行了基准测试，同时评估了ComBat作为一种鲁棒化策略的效果。我们进一步提出了Cramér's V曲线下面积（AUCC）这一指标，以联合衡量绝对分类性能及其随中心相关性增加而出现的性能退化。
tldr: 本文通过受控实验系统量化了类别与采集中心的相关性，首次评估了六种病理学基础模型在全切片图像分类中对中心偏置的鲁棒性，并提出了AUCC指标来联合衡量分类性能及其退化程度，同时验证了ComBat作为鲁棒化策略的有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically evaluates the robustness of six pathology foundation models to center biases in whole-slide image classification under controlled class-center correlations, and introduces the AUCC metric to jointly capture classification performance and its degradation, while assessing ComBat as a robustification strategy.
